--- title: "Object-Oriented Programming in R 🧱" subtitle: "MATH 4750 / MSSC 5750 Computational Statistics" format: revealjs: code-line-numbers: false html-math-method: method: mathjax url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" highlight-style: arrow code-block-bg: true self-contained: false slide-number: c/t incremental: false width: 1800 height: 1000 margin: 0.05 logo: "logo.png" footer: "[mmadoliat.github.io/compstat-s27](https://mmadoliat.github.io/compstat-s27/)" theme: ["simple", "slides.scss"] multiplex: false code-link: true fig-cap-location: bottom fig-align: center transition: none ## fade slide convex concave zoom title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: mu-bg.png data-background-size: stretch data-slide-number: none editor: source execute: freeze: auto echo: true purl: true --- # {visibility="hidden"} \def\bx{\mathbf{x}} \def\by{\mathbf{y}} \def\bz{\mathbf{z}} \def\bu{\mathbf{u}} \def\bv{\mathbf{v}} \def\bw{\mathbf{w}} \def\bX{\mathbf{X}} \def\bY{\mathbf{Y}} \def\bZ{\mathbf{Z}} \def\bU{\mathbf{U}} \def\bV{\mathbf{V}} \def\bW{\mathbf{W}} \def\bI{\mathbf{I}} \def\bH{\mathbf{H}} \def\bS{\mathbf{S}} \def\bD{\mathbf{D}} \def\bbeta{\boldsymbol \beta} \def\btheta{\boldsymbol \theta} \def\bmu{\boldsymbol \mu} \def\bSigma{\boldsymbol \Sigma} \def\bLambda{\boldsymbol \Lambda} \def\beps{\boldsymbol \epsilon} \def\T{\text{T}} \def\E{\mathrm{E}} \def\var{\mathrm{Var}} \def\cov{\mathrm{Cov}} \def\cor{\mathrm{Corr}} \def\se{\mathrm{se}} \def\bias{\mathrm{bias}} \def\mse{\mathrm{MSE}} \def\R{\mathbb{R}} \def\P{\mathrm{P}} \def\iid{\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim}} \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmin}{arg\,min} \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmax}{arg\,max} # Object-Oriented Programming in R

OOP paradigms in R: functional vs. encapsulated

Base types and the S3 system

S4: formal classes

R6: reference semantics

S7 and best practices

::: notes - Adapted from the SCoRT short course (OOP in R) and the course scripts S3.R, S4.R, R6.R, OO-vs-Base.R. Main reference: Hadley Wickham, *Advanced R*, 2nd ed., chapters 12-16. - Running example: we turn the k-NN regression code from deck 03 into a proper class with methods. ::: ## Why OOP in a Statistics Course? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars) par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) plot(mtcars$wt) # a numeric vector -> scatterplot of values plot(iris$Species) # a factor -> barplot plot(fit, which = 1) # an lm object -> residual plot ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/11-oop/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: - **Same function, different behavior** depending on the **class** of the argument: *polymorphism*. - `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()`, `predict()` work on `lm`, `glm`, `boot`, `density`, `hclust`, ... objects. - When you write a new method (an estimator, a resampling procedure), giving it a class lets users use these familiar generics. ## Two Paradigms :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Functional OOP** (S3, S4, S7) - Methods belong to **generic functions** - Call: `generic(object, ...)`, e.g. `summary(fit)` - Objects are (mostly) **immutable**: copy-on-modify ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Encapsulated OOP** (R6, Reference Classes) - Methods belong to **objects** - Call: `object$method(...)`, e.g. `learner$train(task)` - Objects are **mutable**: modified in place ::: :::: ![](images/oop/oo-venn.png){width="40%" fig-align="center"} ## Base Types vs. OO Objects Everything in R is an object, but not every object is object-oriented. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- 1:5; f <- factor(c("a", "b", "c")) c(is.object(x), is.object(f)) # base object vs OO object ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} typeof(f); attributes(f) # an integer vector with a class attribute ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "integer" ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $levels [1] "a" "b" "c" $class [1] "factor" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} unclass(f) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 2 3 attr(,"levels") [1] "a" "b" "c" ``` ::: ::: - Every object has a **base type** (`typeof()`): `"double"`, `"integer"`, `"character"`, `"list"`, `"closure"`, `"environment"`, ... - An OO object has a `class` attribute. # S3: Informal Classes ## S3 Basics - **Lightweight:** no formal definition; an S3 object is a base type with a `class` attribute. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- structure(list(), class = "my_class") # create and assign class in one step y <- list(); class(y) <- "my_class" # create, then set class inherits(x, "my_class") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ::: - Danger: nothing stops you from doing nonsense: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} mod <- lm(log(mpg) ~ log(disp), data = mtcars) class(mod) <- "Date" # turn it into a date (?!) try(print(mod)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Error in as.POSIXlt(.Internal(Date2POSIXlt(x, tz)), tz = tz) : 'list' object cannot be coerced to type 'double' ``` ::: ::: ## Constructor, Validator, Helper ::: instructions 1. **Low-level constructor** `new_myclass()`: assumes inputs are OK; creates the structure efficiently. 2. **Validator** `validate_myclass()`: more expensive checks of the values. 3. **User-facing helper** `myclass()`: coerces/checks inputs, then builds + validates. ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} new_knnreg <- function(x = matrix(numeric()), y = numeric(), k = 1L) { stopifnot(is.matrix(x), is.numeric(y), is.integer(k)) structure(list(x = x, y = y, k = k, center = colMeans(x), scale = apply(x, 2, sd)), class = "knnreg") } validate_knnreg <- function(obj) { if (nrow(obj$x) != length(obj$y)) stop("`x` and `y` must have the same number of observations", call. = FALSE) if (obj$k < 1 || obj$k > nrow(obj$x)) stop("`k` must be between 1 and n", call. = FALSE) if (anyNA(obj$x) || anyNA(obj$y)) stop("missing values are not allowed", call. = FALSE) obj } knnreg <- function(x, y, k = 5) { validate_knnreg(new_knnreg(as.matrix(x), as.numeric(y), as.integer(k))) } ``` ::: ## Generics and Method Dispatch - A **generic** calls `UseMethod()`, which looks for `generic.class`, then `generic.default`: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} print ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` function (x, ...) UseMethod("print") ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} predict ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` function (object, ...) UseMethod("predict") ``` ::: ::: - `print(x)` with `class(x) = c("ordered", "factor")` tries `print.ordered` $\rightarrow$ `print.factor` $\rightarrow$ `print.default`. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} sloop::s3_dispatch(print(ordered("x"))) sloop::s3_methods_class("hclust") ``` ::: ## Creating Methods for `knnreg` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} print.knnreg <- function(x, ...) { cat("k-NN regression with k =", x$k, "\n") cat("n =", nrow(x$x), "observations, p =", ncol(x$x), "predictors\n") invisible(x) } predict.knnreg <- function(object, newdata = object$x, k = object$k, ...) { tr <- scale(object$x, object$center, object$scale) te <- scale(as.matrix(newdata), object$center, object$scale) apply(te, 1, function(x0) mean(object$y[order(colSums((t(tr) - x0)^2))[1:k]])) } fit <- knnreg(mtcars[, c("wt", "qsec")], mtcars$mpg, k = 5) fit ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` k-NN regression with k = 5 n = 32 observations, p = 2 predictors ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(wt = c(2, 3.5), qsec = c(20, 17))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 27.58 17.18 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} try(knnreg(mtcars[, c("wt", "qsec")], mtcars$mpg, k = 100)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Error : `k` must be between 1 and n ``` ::: ::: ## A New Generic ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} cv_error <- function(object, ...) UseMethod("cv_error") # the generic cv_error.knnreg <- function(object, ks = 1:15, folds = 5, ...) { n <- nrow(object$x); fold <- sample(rep(1:folds, length.out = n)) sapply(ks, function(k) mean(sapply(1:folds, function(f) { sub <- knnreg(object$x[fold != f, , drop = FALSE], object$y[fold != f], k) mean((object$y[fold == f] - predict(sub, object$x[fold == f, , drop = FALSE]))^2) }))) } set.seed(4750) plot(1:15, cv_error(fit), type = "b", pch = 19, xlab = "k", ylab = "5-fold CV error") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/11-oop/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Inheritance and `NextMethod()` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # a weighted version: closer neighbors get larger weights wknnreg <- function(x, y, k = 5) { obj <- knnreg(x, y, k) class(obj) <- c("wknnreg", class(obj)) # subclass first obj } print.wknnreg <- function(x, ...) { cat("(distance-weighted) ") NextMethod() # then call print.knnreg } wfit <- wknnreg(mtcars[, c("wt", "qsec")], mtcars$mpg, k = 5) class(wfit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "wknnreg" "knnreg" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} wfit ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (distance-weighted) k-NN regression with k = 5 n = 32 observations, p = 2 predictors ``` ::: ::: ::: question We did not write `predict.wknnreg()`. Which method will `predict(wfit, ...)` use? Write the weighted version. ::: ## S3 for Things You Already Use ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} methods(class = "density") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] coerce initialize plot print show slotsFromS3 see '?methods' for accessing help and source code ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} d <- density(faithful$eruptions) class(d); names(d) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "density" ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "x" "y" "bw" "n" "call" "data.name" [7] "has.na" ``` ::: ::: - `boot()` (Ch 8), `density()` (Ch 12), `hclust()` (clustering), `optim()` (Ch 14) all return objects with methods; reading the method source is the best way to learn what they compute: `getS3method("print", "density")`. # S4: Formal Classes ## S4: Classes with Slots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} setClass("KNNReg", slots = c(x = "matrix", y = "numeric", k = "integer"), validity = function(object) { if (nrow(object@x) != length(object@y)) return("x and y have different numbers of rows") if (object@k < 1L) return("k must be positive") TRUE }) m4 <- new("KNNReg", x = as.matrix(mtcars[, c("wt", "qsec")]), y = mtcars$mpg, k = 5L) m4@k # slot access via @ ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} slot(m4, "k") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} isVirtualClass("KNNReg") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] FALSE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} try(new("KNNReg", x = matrix(1:4, 2), y = 1:3, k = 1L)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Error in validObject(.Object) : invalid class "KNNReg" object: x and y have different numbers of rows ``` ::: ::: ## S4 Generics and Methods ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} setGeneric("fitted_knn", function(object, ...) standardGeneric("fitted_knn")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "fitted_knn" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} setMethod("fitted_knn", "KNNReg", function(object, ...) { X <- scale(object@x) apply(X, 1, function(x0) mean(object@y[order(colSums((t(X) - x0)^2))[1:object@k]])) }) setMethod("show", "KNNReg", function(object) { cat(" k =", object@k, " n =", nrow(object@x), "\n") }) m4 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` k = 5 n = 32 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(fitted_knn(m4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Mazda RX4 Mazda RX4 Wag Datsun 710 Hornet 4 Drive 21.28 18.28 26.86 20.62 Hornet Sportabout Valiant 17.18 20.64 ``` ::: ::: ## S4 Inheritance and Multiple Dispatch ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} setClass("WKNNReg", contains = "KNNReg", slots = c(power = "numeric")) w4 <- new("WKNNReg", m4, power = 2) is(w4, "KNNReg") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] TRUE ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} w4 # inherits show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` k = 5 n = 32 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} setGeneric("combine", function(a, b) standardGeneric("combine")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "combine" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} setMethod("combine", signature("KNNReg", "numeric"), function(a, b) "model + number") setMethod("combine", signature("numeric", "KNNReg"), function(a, b) "number + model") c(combine(m4, 1), combine(1, m4)) # dispatch on BOTH arguments ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "model + number" "number + model" ``` ::: ::: - S4 is used heavily in Bioconductor and in `Matrix`, `lme4`, ... # R6: Reference Semantics ## R6 Classes ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(R6) Accumulator <- R6Class("Accumulator", list( sum = 0, add = function(x = 1) { self$sum <- self$sum + x invisible(self) # return self to allow method chaining }) ) x <- Accumulator$new() x$add(4) x$sum ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x$add(10)$add(10)$sum ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 24 ``` ::: ::: ## Reference Semantics: Objects Are Not Copied ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} y1 <- Accumulator$new() y2 <- y1 # NOT a copy: same object y1$add(10) c(y1 = y1$sum, y2 = y2$sum) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` y1 y2 10 10 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} y3 <- y1$clone() # an explicit copy y1$add(5); c(y1 = y1$sum, y3 = y3$sum) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` y1 y3 15 10 ``` ::: ::: - Contrast with S3/S4 where `y2 <- y1; modify(y1)` leaves `y2` unchanged. ## An R6 Online Learner ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} RunningMoments <- R6Class("RunningMoments", public = list( initialize = function() invisible(self), update = function(x) { # Welford's algorithm (Ch 13: numerically stable) for (xi in x) { private$n <- private$n + 1 delta <- xi - private$mu private$mu <- private$mu + delta / private$n private$m2 <- private$m2 + delta * (xi - private$mu) } invisible(self) }, print = function(...) cat("n =", private$n, " mean =", private$mu, " var =", self$var, "\n") ), private = list(n = 0, mu = 0, m2 = 0), active = list(var = function() private$m2 / (private$n - 1)) ) set.seed(4750); rm1 <- RunningMoments$new() rm1$update(rnorm(1000))$update(rnorm(1000, 1)); rm1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` n = 2000 mean = 0.5018 var = 1.254 ``` ::: ::: ## R6 Features :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} - `public`, `private`, and `active` fields - `initialize()` constructor, `print()` method - Inheritance: `R6Class("Child", inherit = Parent)`, `super$method()` - `clone(deep = TRUE)` - Used by `shiny` (sessions), `mlr3`, `torch`, `httr2` ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ![](images/oop/R6_Features.png){width="100%"} ::: :::: ## S7: The New OOP System - Designed by the R Consortium to unify S3 + S4 and fix their issues: formal properties, validation, multiple dispatch, S3/S4 compatibility. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(S7) Circle <- new_class("Circle", properties = list(radius = class_double)) area <- new_generic("area", "shape") method(area, Circle) <- function(shape) pi * shape@radius^2 c1 <- Circle(radius = 5) c1 area(c1) ``` ::: ## Trade-offs and Best Practices | Paradigm | Pros | Cons | |----------|------|------| | S3 | Simple, flexible, ubiquitous | No schema, fragile dispatch | | S4 | Formal, robust, multiple dispatch | Verbose, steeper learning curve | | R6 | Encapsulated, mutable, fast | Not idiomatic for most stats objects | | S7 | Unified, type-safe | Newer, evolving ecosystem | ::: instructions - For a statistical method: **S3** with constructor/validator/helper + `print`, `summary`, `predict`, `plot` methods. - Use **R6** when state must change in place (simulations, online algorithms, apps). - Document constructors and methods; write unit tests (next lecture: R packages). ::: ::: your-turn Write an S3 class `mcint` returned by `mc_integrate(g, a, b, m)` (Ch 6) with `print` (estimate and SE) and `plot` (running mean with $\pm 2$ SE bands) methods. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
